stem: $X=\{ {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3} \}$ and $Y=\{ {=y1}, {=y2}, {=y3}, {=y4} \}$. Which of the following relations from $X$ to $Y$ is a function?
solution: A relation from $X$ to $Y$ is a function when every element of $X$ has exactly one image in $Y$, so each of {=x1}, {=x2} and {=x3} must appear as a first element exactly once.
$\{ {=optok} \}$ has {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3} each once as a first element, so it is a function.
$\{ {=optA} \}$ is not a function: {=x1} has two images, {=f1} and {=g1}.
$\{ {=optB} \}$ is not a function: {=x3} has no image.
$\{ {=optC} \}$ is not a function: {=x2} has two images, {=f2} and {=g2}.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Allows an element of X with two images
proposed_misconceptions.description: Accepts a relation as a function although some element of X has more than one arrow/pair.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Allows an element of X with no image
proposed_misconceptions.description: Accepts a relation as a function even though some element of X is not the first element of any pair.

notes: Correct option and distractors are built from the same pairs; each distractor breaks exactly the one-image rule. Ys are sampled, f's drawn from ys (f1 choice list is filtered by require, so some attempts are discarded; acceptable). Stem varies via X and Y holes.
